items.question: What is opportunity cost, and why does it matter when you decide?
items.answer: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative you give up when you choose one option over another. It is not the price you pay, but what that same money, time or attention could have done for you elsewhere. Weighing it turns every choice into a comparison of real options, rather than a verdict on one option alone.

resources.title: The road not taken
resources.body:
Picture two roads.
The one you take has a price; the one you leave behind is the cost.

items.answer: Giving up some of one thing to get more of another

items.question: Why should a sunk cost not sway a new decision?
